featured_charts.title: A World of Debt
featured_charts.description: Developing countries' public debt continues to grow. The main problem is the cost. They pay far higher interest rates than developed countries. In many, interest bills now exceed spending on health or education.

stats.label: Global public debt has more than doubled since 2010, reaching $111 trillion in 2025.
Their rates reach 5.2%, against 2.2% for developed countries. They paid nearly $1 trillion in interest in 2025.
stats.lead: Developing countries pay far more to borrow.

stats.label: Today, 3.7 billion people live in countries that spend more on interest than on health or education, putting essential services at risk.

stats.lead: External finance is harder to access.
stats.label: Bilateral lenders are diverting aid, and private creditors are more risk averse.

quote.text: This is not a debt crisis. It’s a development crisis. Countries face an impossible choice: to default on their debt or default on their development.
quote.name: Rebeca Grynspan
quote.title: Secretary-General of UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD)

solutions.title: UNCTAD’s work on debt
description: Governments use public debt to finance public services and infrastructure, protect and invest in their people and build a better future.
But when interest costs rise too high, people’s futures are at risk. This is the reality facing a growing number of developing countries.
Today, 3.7 billion people live in countries spending more on interest payments than on health or education.

borrowers_platform.title: No country can solve the debt crisis alone
borrowers_platform.description: UNCTAD is the secretariat of the Borrowers’ Platform, a member state-led initiative of finance ministers and central bank governors. It offers borrowing countries a dedicated space to come together, share knowledge, learn from each other and speak collectively on debt issues.

stats.label: Chairs the first annual cycle, from October 2026 to October 2027

quote.text: We undertake to develop a global and representative membership of borrowing countries committed to improving debt sustainability practices and development-oriented finance, and to strengthen cooperation among borrowing countries in support of a fairer, more responsive and more equitable international debt architecture.
quote.name: Borrowers’ Platform

dmfas_highlight.title: Over 40 years building countries’ capacity to manage national debt
dmfas_highlight.description: Until recently, South Sudan tracked its loans in spreadsheets. In 2025, it became the second country, after Zambia, to install the latest version of UNCTAD's debt management software. The DMFAS programme also trains debt officers and advises governments, so borrowing decisions rest on reliable data.
